titre: L'incident d'ingestion du 12/11 : cause, absence de perte et suites, à croiser entre Slack, le postmortem et Linear

entree.question: What actually broke in the event pipeline last Thursday? Did we lose any customer data, and what are we changing so it doesn't happen again?

faits.texte: Says the cause was the ingest v2.14.0 deploy, which raised the default batch size (max_batch_bytes) from 1 MB to 10 MB, so the workers ran out of memory and crash-looped.
Says no events or customer data were lost: they were processed late (checked by the reconciliation of November 13).
Says dashboards were delayed for about 3h40 (08:47 to 12:27 UTC on November 12).
Mentions the alert on consumer lag above 5 minutes (KES-431, Noa) and says it is not finished yet (threshold still being tuned).
Mentions that ingest configuration changes will go to a canary pool first (KES-432, Daniel).
Mentions raising the worker memory limit and adding a load test on batch sizes (KES-433, Lior).
Says it was fixed by rolling back to v2.13.3 (the default was then reverted in ingest#419).
Says detection took 27 minutes because there was no alert on consumer lag.

interdits.texte: Says events or customer data were lost.
Gives the Kafka brokers' disk as the cause (an early hypothesis, ruled out at 09:41).
Says the consumer-lag alert follow-up is complete.
Blames the database or the Postgres upgrade for the incident.

pieges: Croiser : la cause est dans Slack et le postmortem, l'absence de perte dans la réconciliation du 13/11, l'état réel des suites dans Linear (KES-431 pas fini alors que le postmortem le donne pour le 20/11).
Fausse piste : « Kafka broker disk ? » lancé à 09:26, écarté à 09:41.
Vocabulaire : « event pipeline », « last Thursday » (le 12/11) au lieu de ingest, incident, SEV2 ; la date relative se lit depuis le mercredi 18/11.
